title: Normality and density of the localized relative normalization
statement: Let $S$ be an integral Noetherian quasi-separated scheme whose local rings are integrally closed [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $c:C\to S$ be quasi-compact, quasi-separated and smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $U\subset S$ be open, $P\to C_U=c^{-1}(U)$ a finite etale scheme [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category], and $s\in S$. Put $f:P\to C_U\to C$, $L=C\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{S,s}$ with projection $l:L\to C$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and $n:N=f.\mathrm{normalization}\times_C L\to L$, where relative normalization means integral closure of $\mathcal O_C$ in $f_*\mathcal O_P$ [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization]. Then each local ring of $N$ is a domain and integrally closed, and $n^{-1}(l^{-1}(C_U))$ is dense in $N$. No finiteness hypothesis on $n$, boundary minimality, fibre neighbourhood, generic-point membership, or geometric connectedness is required.

proof.text: Smoothness over the normal integral base gives normal local rings of C; etaleness gives normal local rings of P. Both are locally Noetherian, so quasi-compact opens of P have finitely many irreducible components.

Apply the affine integral-closure construction and Tag 035L: decompose the source over each affine chart into its finitely many normal integral components. Each ring of sections is a normal domain. Its integral closure over the base algebra is a normal domain, so all local rings of the relative normalization are normal domains. Choose an affine neighbourhood of s; base change to its stalk is localization of the base algebra. Integral closure commutes with this localization (0307), proving the same property after the displayed base change. The affine descriptions agree on overlaps.

The inclusion of the integral-closure algebra into the rings of sections makes P to its relative normalization schematically dominant (035I). Localization is flat, so this inclusion remains injective after base change to the stalk. Thus the localized source has dense image in N. That image lies over C_U, which proves density of the displayed open; when P is empty N is empty and density is vacuous.

theorem stalk_normalization_normal_and_dense {S C : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsNoetherian S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] [IsIntegral S]
    (hS : ∀ x : S, IsIntegrallyClosed (S.presheaf.stalk x))
    (c : C ⟶ S) [QuasiCompact c] [QuasiSeparated c] [Smooth c]
    (U : S.Opens)
    (PA : (c ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme.FiniteEtale)
    (s : S) :
    letI : IsFinite PA.obj.hom := PA.property
    letI : QuasiCompact (c ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι :=
      MorphismProperty.of_isPullback (isPullback_morphismRestrict c U)
        (inferInstance : QuasiCompact U.ι)
    let f := PA.obj.hom ≫ (c ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι
    let l := pullback.fst c (S.fromSpecStalk s)
    let n := pullback.snd f.fromNormalization l
    (∀ z : (pullback f.fromNormalization l : Scheme.{u}),
      IsDomain ((pullback f.fromNormalization l : Scheme.{u}).presheaf.stalk z) ∧
      IsIntegrallyClosed ((pullback f.fromNormalization l : Scheme.{u}).presheaf.stalk z)) ∧
    Dense (↑(n ⁻¹ᵁ (l ⁻¹ᵁ (c ⁻¹ᵁ U))) :
      Set (pullback f.fromNormalization l : Scheme.{u}))
